title: Validate Binary Search Tree

statement.hi:
Binary tree ka `root` diya hai. Batao ki ye ek **valid BST** hai ya nahi.

Valid BST: har node ke **left subtree** ki saari values node se **strictly chhoti**, **right subtree** ki saari values **strictly badi**, aur dono subtrees bhi khud valid BST hon.
statement.en:
Given the `root` of a binary tree, determine whether it is a **valid binary search tree**.

A valid BST: every value in a node’s **left subtree** is **strictly less** than the node’s value, every value in its **right subtree** is **strictly greater**, and both subtrees are valid BSTs too.

hi: Sirf parent se compare karna kaafi nahi — poore subtree ka khayal rakhna hai.
Har node ke liye ek allowed range `(lo, hi)` pass karo. Ya inorder traversal strictly increasing hona chahiye.
Values INT_MIN/INT_MAX tak ja sakti hain — bounds ke liye `long long` ya pointers use karo.
en: Comparing with the parent alone is not enough — the whole subtree matters.
Pass an allowed range `(lo, hi)` down to every node. Alternatively, the inorder traversal must be strictly increasing.
Values can reach INT_MIN/INT_MAX — use `long long` or node pointers for the bounds.

explain.hi: Root 5 hai lekin right child 4 hai, jo 5 se chhota hai.
explain.en: The root is 5 but its right child is 4, which is smaller.

approach.hi:
DFS with bounds: `check(node, lo, hi)` — node ki value `lo < val < hi` honi chahiye; left me `(lo, val)` aur right me `(val, hi)` pass karo.
Bounds `long long` me rakho (LLONG_MIN/LLONG_MAX) taaki INT_MIN/INT_MAX values bhi sahi chalein. O(n) time, O(h) space.
approach.en:
DFS with bounds: `check(node, lo, hi)` — the value must satisfy `lo < val < hi`; pass `(lo, val)` to the left and `(val, hi)` to the right.
Keep the bounds in `long long` (LLONG_MIN/LLONG_MAX) so INT_MIN/INT_MAX values work. O(n) time, O(h) space.
